def-milstein-scheme-and-iterated-integra:
## Definition

Assume AC and the Brownian filtered-space conventions in [[def-continuous-brownian-ito-process]]. Let $d,m\ge1$ be finite integers, let $W=(W^1,\ldots,W^m)$ be the driving standard Brownian motion, and consider the autonomous It\^o SDE
$$dX_t=b(X_t)\,dt+\sum_{j=1}^m\sigma_j(X_t)\,dW^j_t,$$
where $b:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d$ and $\sigma_j:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d$. For a differentiable vector-valued function $f$, $Df(x)$ is its Jacobian and $L_i f(x):=Df(x)\sigma_i(x)$; this definition is applied componentwise when $f$ is matrix-valued.

On a deterministic grid $t_n=nh$, define $\Delta W_n^j=W^j_{t_{n+1}}-W^j_{t_n}$ and the iterated It\^o integral
$$I_{ij,n}:=\int_{t_n}^{t_{n+1}}(W^i_s-W^i_{t_n})\,dW^j_s,\qquad 1\le i,j\le m.$$
The integrand is predictable and square-integrable, so this is the $L^2$ It\^o integral of [[def-ito-integral-for-square-integrable-predictable-processes]]; its finite energy is $\mathbb E\int_{t_n}^{t_{n+1}}(W^i_s-W^i_{t_n})^2ds=h^2/2$ by [[thm-ito-isometry-and-linearity-in-predictable-l2]].

The general Milstein Taylor update is
$$Y_{n+1}=Y_n+b(Y_n)h+\sum_{j=1}^m\sigma_j(Y_n)\Delta W_n^j+\sum_{i,j=1}^m L_i\sigma_j(Y_n)I_{ij,n}.$$
The diffusion fields have **commutative noise** when $L_i\sigma_j(x)=L_j\sigma_i(x)$ for every $x$ and every $i,j$. Under that condition, the equivalent update using only Brownian increments is
$$Y_{n+1}=Y_n+b(Y_n)h+\sum_{j=1}^m\sigma_j(Y_n)\Delta W_n^j+\frac12\sum_{i,j=1}^m L_i\sigma_j(Y_n)\bigl(\Delta W_n^i\Delta W_n^j-\delta_{ij}h\bigr).$$
For scalar noise ($d=m=1$), this reads
$$Y_{n+1}=Y_n+b(Y_n)h+\sigma(Y_n)\Delta W_n+\frac12\sigma(Y_n)\sigma'(Y_n)\bigl((\Delta W_n)^2-h\bigr).$$

For $i\ne j$, define the Brownian area component $A_{ij,n}:=(I_{ij,n}-I_{ji,n})/2$ and the symmetric part $S_{ij,n}:=(I_{ij,n}+I_{ji,n})/2$. Then $A_{ji,n}=-A_{ij,n}$, $S_{ji,n}=S_{ij,n}$, and reindexing the sums gives
$$\sum_{i,j}L_i\sigma_j I_{ij,n}=\frac12\sum_{i,j}(L_i\sigma_j+L_j\sigma_i)S_{ij,n}+\frac12\sum_{i,j}(L_i\sigma_j-L_j\sigma_i)A_{ij,n}.$$
The second sum vanishes under commutative noise; otherwise the general update includes the area components. A noncommuting Milstein implementation must sample or approximate the needed areas and account for their approximation error and computational cost; this definition makes no claim that an exact area sample is free or that a particular area sampler has a specified error rate.

For this pair, $C_b^k(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb R^q)$ means that every component and every partial derivative of orders at most $k$ exists, is continuous, and is bounded. This notation is componentwise for vector and matrix valued functions.
lem-iterated-brownian-integral-identitie:
## Statement

Let the finite-dimensional Brownian It\^o setting and the integrals $I_{ij,n}$ be as in [[def-milstein-scheme-and-iterated-integrals]]. For every grid interval of length $h>0$,
$$I_{ij,n}+I_{ji,n}=\Delta W_n^i\Delta W_n^j-\delta_{ij}h.$$
In the scalar case, writing $I_n=I_{11,n}$ and $\Delta W_n=\Delta W_n^1$, this gives
$$I_n=\frac12\bigl((\Delta W_n)^2-h\bigr),\quad \mathbb E[I_n\mid\mathcal F_{t_n}]=0,\quad \mathbb E[I_n^2\mid\mathcal F_{t_n}]=\frac{h^2}{2},\quad \mathbb E[\Delta W_n I_n\mid\mathcal F_{t_n}]=0.$$
Consequently, under the commutativity condition in the Definition, the double-integral term in the general Milstein Taylor increment equals
$$\sum_{i,j}L_i\sigma_j(Y_n)I_{ij,n}=\frac12\sum_{i,j}L_i\sigma_j(Y_n)\bigl(\Delta W_n^i\Delta W_n^j-\delta_{ij}h\bigr).$$
lem-event-weighted-ito-isometry:
## Statement

Assume AC and the Brownian filtration conventions in [[def-continuous-brownian-ito-process]]. Let $t\ge0$, $h>0$, let $A\in\mathcal F_t$, and let $H$ be a real predictable process with finite energy on $[t,t+h]$ and $H_s=0$ for $s\notin(t,t+h]$. For any coordinate $W^j$ of the driving finite-dimensional Brownian motion,
$$\mathbb E\!\left[\mathbf1_A\left|\int_t^{t+h}H_s\,dW_s^j\right|^2\right]=\mathbb E\!\left[\mathbf1_A\int_t^{t+h}|H_s|^2\,ds\right].$$
lem-bounded-sde-increment-moments:
## Statement

Let $X$ solve the autonomous SDE in [[def-milstein-scheme-and-iterated-integrals]] on a filtered probability space with an $m$-dimensional Brownian motion relative to the filtration. Assume $b,\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_m\in C_b^3(\mathbb R^d)$, with the $C_b^3$ convention of the Definition. There is a constant $C$ depending only on the coefficient bounds and $d,m$ such that for every $t\ge0$, $0\le r\le1$, and $A\in\mathcal F_t$,
$$\mathbb E\!\left[\mathbf1_A|X_{t+r}-X_t|^2\right]\le Cr\,P(A),\qquad \mathbb E\!\left[\mathbf1_A|X_{t+r}-X_t|^4\right]\le Cr^2\,P(A).$$
These event-weighted inequalities are the conditional second- and fourth-moment bounds for the increment.
lem-milstein-local-defect-bounds:
## Statement

Let $X$ solve the finite-dimensional autonomous SDE in [[def-milstein-scheme-and-iterated-integrals]] with $b,\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_m\in C_b^3(\mathbb R^d)$, using the $C_b^3$ convention in that Definition. Let $0<h\le1$ and let $[t,t+h]$ be a deterministic interval. Define $L_0f:=Df\,b+\frac12\sum_{k=1}^mD^2f[\sigma_k,\sigma_k]$ and $L_if:=Df\,\sigma_i$ for $i\ge1$. Then there is a remainder $R_{t,h}\in L^2(\mathbb R^d)$ such that
$$X_{t+h}=X_t+b(X_t)h+\sum_{j=1}^m\sigma_j(X_t)\Delta W^j+\sum_{i,j=1}^mL_i\sigma_j(X_t)I_{ij}+R_{t,h},$$
where $\Delta W^j=W^j_{t+h}-W^j_t$ and $I_{ij}=\int_t^{t+h}(W_s^i-W_t^i)dW_s^j$. Moreover, for the conditioning sigma algebra $\mathcal F_t$ there is a conditional-expectation version $r_{t,h}=\mathbb E[R_{t,h}\mid\mathcal F_t]$ with
$$|r_{t,h}|\le Ch^2,\qquad \mathbb E[|R_{t,h}|^2\mid\mathcal F_t]\le Ch^3\quad\text{almost surely},$$
where $C$ depends only on $d,m$ and the coefficient bounds, not on $t,h$ or $X_t$.
lem-stochastic-local-to-global-rms-bound:
## Statement

Let $N\ge1$, $0<h\le1$, and $Nh\le T$. Let $(\mathcal F_n)_{n=0}^N$ be a filtration as in [[def-filtration-and-filtered-probability-space]]. For every $n$, let $e_n,u_n,r_n$ be square-integrable $\mathbb R^d$-valued, $\mathcal F_n$-measurable random vectors; let $M_{n+1},Q_{n+1}$ be square-integrable and $\mathcal F_{n+1}$-measurable. Say $Z$ is orthogonal to $\mathcal F_n$ if $\mathbb E\langle H,Z\rangle=0$ for every square-integrable $\mathcal F_n$-measurable vector $H$. Suppose
$$e_0=0,\quad e_{n+1}=e_n+hu_n+r_n+M_{n+1}+Q_{n+1},$$
$$|u_n|\le L|e_n|,\qquad |r_n|\le C_0h^2,$$
and $M_{n+1},Q_{n+1}$ are orthogonal to $\mathcal F_n$, with
$$\mathbb E|M_{n+1}|^2\le C_1h\,\mathbb E|e_n|^2,\qquad \mathbb E|Q_{n+1}|^2\le C_1h^3.$$
Then $\mathbb E|e_N|^2\le C_T h^2$, where $C_T$ depends only on $T,L,C_0,C_1$ and not on $h$ or $N$. This is a local-to-global estimate for an order-one grid RMS error when the drift error is Lipschitz and the centered one-step defect has second moment $O(h^3)$.
thm-commutative-milstein-strong-order-on:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $d,m\ge1$ be finite, let $W$ be an $m$-dimensional Brownian motion relative to a filtration satisfying [[def-continuous-brownian-ito-process]], and let $X$ solve
$$dX_t=b(X_t)dt+\sum_{j=1}^m\sigma_j(X_t)dW_t^j,\qquad X_0\in L^2(\mathbb R^d).$$
Assume $b,\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_m\in C_b^3(\mathbb R^d)$ as defined in [[def-milstein-scheme-and-iterated-integrals]]. Put $L_i f=Df\,\sigma_i$ and assume commutative noise $L_i\sigma_j=L_j\sigma_i$ for all $i,j$. On the uniform grid $t_n=nh$, $h=T/N\le1$, initialize $Y_0=X_0$ and use the product-increment Milstein update in the Definition. Then there is a constant $C_T$, independent of $N$, such that
$$\max_{0\le n\le N}\mathbb E|Y_n-X_{t_n}|^2\le C_T h^2.$$
Thus the grid root-mean-square error is $O(h)$ on $[0,T]$. For $m=1$ the commutativity condition is automatic and the scheme is the scalar Milstein update. No claim is made for a noncommuting-noise scheme without an area sampler satisfying a separately proved approximation bound.
def-additive-noise-stochastic-heun-schem:
## Definition

Assume AC and the Brownian filtered-space conventions in [[def-continuous-brownian-ito-process]]. Consider the scalar additive-noise It\^o SDE
$$dX_t=b(X_t)\,dt+\sigma\,dW_t,$$
where $\sigma\in\mathbb R$ is constant. Given a step size $h>0$, a grid value $Y_n$, and the Brownian increment $\Delta W_n=W_{t_{n+1}}-W_{t_n}$, the explicit stochastic Heun update is the two-stage rule
$$Z_n=Y_n+b(Y_n)h+\sigma\Delta W_n,\qquad Y_{n+1}=Y_n+\frac h2\bigl(b(Y_n)+b(Z_n)\bigr)+\sigma\Delta W_n.$$
The predictor $Z_n$ uses the same increment as the corrector. One step evaluates $b$ at $Y_n$ and $Z_n$ and uses one Gaussian increment. The weak order-two guarantee authored in this pair is only for this constant-diffusion scheme; the displayed update omits terms required for the corresponding multiplicative-noise guarantee.

In this definition and its consumers, $C_b^k(\mathbb R;\mathbb R)$ means that the function and all its derivatives through order $k$ are continuous and bounded.
lem-additive-heun-one-step-weak-expansio:
## Statement

Let $b\in C_b^6(\mathbb R;\mathbb R)$, let $\sigma\in\mathbb R$ be constant, and define the generator $Lf=b f'+\frac12\sigma^2f''$. Let $u:[0,T]\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ satisfy $u_t+Lu=0$. Assume all mixed derivatives $\partial_t^r\partial_x^j u$ for $0\le r\le3$ and $0\le j\le6$ are continuous and bounded. For $0<h\le1$, $t+h\le T$, fixed $x\in\mathbb R$, and $w\sim N(0,h)$, take one Heun step from [[def-additive-noise-stochastic-heun-scheme]] and let $D=Y_{n+1}-x$. Then a constant $C$, uniform in $t,x,h$, satisfies
$$\left|\mathbb E\bigl[u(t+h,x+D)\bigr]-u(t,x)\right|\le Ch^3.$$
thm-additive-noise-stochastic-heun-weak-:
## Statement

Assume AC and the Brownian filtration conventions in [[def-continuous-brownian-ito-process]]. Consider $dX_t=b(X_t)dt+\sigma dW_t$ on $[0,T]$, where $b\in C_b^6(\mathbb R;\mathbb R)$, $\sigma\in\mathbb R$ is constant, and $X_0=x_0\in\mathbb R$ is deterministic. For $t\le T$ and $x\in\mathbb R$, let $X^{t,x}$ denote the solution of the same SDE started from $x$ at time $t$. Let $\phi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ have a bounded classical backward solution $u(t,x)=\mathbb E[\phi(X_T^{t,x})]$ with $u(T,x)=\phi(x)$, $u_t+Lu=0$, $L=b\partial_x+\frac12\sigma^2\partial_{xx}$, and all mixed derivatives $\partial_t^r\partial_x^j u$ for $0\le r\le3$ and $0\le j\le6$ continuous and bounded. On a uniform grid $h=T/N\le1$, initialize $Y_0=x_0$ and apply the additive-noise stochastic Heun update in [[def-additive-noise-stochastic-heun-scheme]]. There is a constant $C_T$, independent of $h$, such that
$$\left|\mathbb E\phi(Y_N)-\mathbb E\phi(X_T)\right|\le C_T h^2.$$
This is weak order two, meaning the expectation error is bounded by a constant times $h^2$ for the stated payoff class. The claim is specific to constant additive diffusion; no multiplicative-noise order-two result is asserted.
thm-milstein-mlmc-level-variance-and-cos:
## Statement

Assume AC and the scalar or commutative-noise SDE hypotheses of [[thm-commutative-milstein-strong-order-one]]. Let $T>0$, use dyadic step sizes $h_\ell=T2^{-\ell}$, and let $\psi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ be Lipschitz. At each level form the Milstein approximation $Y_\ell(T)$; couple adjacent levels by using the same Brownian path, so each coarse increment is the sum of its two fine increments. Put $P_\ell=\psi(Y_\ell(T))$ and let $\Delta_\ell=P_\ell^f-P_{\ell-1}^c$ for $\ell\ge1$, as in [[def-mlmc-hierarchy-and-coupled-corrections]]. For fixed finite $d,m$ and bounded-cost coefficient and derivative evaluations, constants independent of $\ell$ satisfy
$$|\mathbb E P_\ell-\mathbb E\psi(X_T)|\le C_bh_\ell,\qquad \operatorname{Var}(\Delta_\ell)\le C_vh_\ell^2,\qquad C_\ell\le C_ch_\ell^{-1}.$$
The exact statement and proof of [[thm-mlmc-complexity-under-rate-assumptions]] then give an MLMC estimator with root-mean-square error at most $\epsilon$ and total work $O(\epsilon^{-2})$ for all sufficiently small $\epsilon>0$. The variance statement is for Lipschitz terminal payoffs and the stated nested coupling; no Euler correction-rate theorem or area-sampling cost is substituted.
